newsitem.title: USA: GE posts record profit for second quarter.
newsitem.headline: GE posts record profit for second quarter.

text.p: General Electric Co. said on Thursday that its profits soared to a record of $2.16 billion in the second quarter as most of its global businesses registered strong growth.

The giant manufacturing and broadcasting company said its net income for the three months ended June 30 rose 13 percent to $2.162 billion, or 66 cents a share, from $1.908 billion, or 58 cents a share.

GE said its second-quarter revenues, including those from acquisitions, rose 15 percent to a record $22 billion from $19.1 billion, helped by higher sales of spare parts and services by its equipment businesses.

"The quarter's double-digit increase again demonstrates the ability of GE's diverse mix of leading global businesses to deliver top-line growth, increased margins and strong cash generation," Chairman John F. Welch said in a statement.
"These strong second-quarter results position GE to deliver another year of record performance in 1997."
The company, which is based in Fairfield, Conn., also said its second-quarter operating margin increased to a record 17.1 percent of sales, up from last year's 16.3 percent.
It said the increase was the 16th consecutive quarterly increase in operating margin and reflected GE's ongoing emphasis on productivity and benefits from its "Six Sigma" quality initiative.

The company said 10 of its 12 businesses reported higher operating profit for the quarter, with nine -- led by GE Capital Services, NBC and its aircraft engines unit -- achieving double-digit increases.
It said GE Capital Services' earnings expanded by 17 percent to $798 million from $683 million, benefiting from the globalization and diversity of the unit's 27 businesses.
For the first six months of the year, GE said, net income rose 12 percent to $3.84 billion, or $1.17 cents a share, from $3.43 billion, or $1.03 cents a share.
Revenues climbed to $42.15 billion from $36.16 billion.
GE's stock gained 68.75 cents to $69.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
